result.summary: The supplied evidence is mostly tests, fixtures and the draft-test controllers. The production mutation controllers, removal confirmation, session service and transport lane are absent, so most assigned obligations are could-not-verify. I found one low-severity defect: the Kotlin draft test has no handling for a rejected-outcome reply. TypeScript shows a specific failure message in that case, while Kotlin falls through to a misleading "unavailable / retry after cleanup" state. Nothing was executed. Stale-tuple and drain-ownership logic in the supplied draft-test controllers looks consistent across both languages.

findings.trigger: The daemon returns a MutationOutcome-shaped rejection for a draft test (e.g. invalid-input for a file path outside the repository, conflict, not-found, secret-unavailable) and the user presses Test in the JetBrains manager.
findings.defect: Kotlin has no rejected-outcome branch. The reply goes through ConnectionProtocol.testResult, which expects a DraftTestResult carrying requestId/draftRevision/daemonEpoch. A rejection therefore parses to null and is published as 'unavailable' with cleanupUnverified=true. The reservation also stays in the map, which counts toward the 128 limit. TypeScript decodes the rejection, shows a code-specific message, and drops the reservation when the rejection is not uncertain. The Kotlin result is a misleading 'Retry after cleanup completes.' message for a permanent input error, which breaks parity with TypeScript (plan t15 requires the same Test behaviour as TypeScript).
findings.evidence: test-controller.ts decodes via decodeMutationOutcome and rejectedMessages, then deletes the slot when !uncertain. ConnectionDraftTests.kt:79 uses only runCatching{ConnectionProtocol.testResult(...)}.getOrNull(), and line 84 maps parsed==null to publish("unavailable",true). ConnectionDraftTestsTest corrupts only requestId/draftRevision/repoRoot/daemonEpoch/safeMessage and never sends a rejected outcome. ConnectionProtocol itself is not supplied, so I assumed testResult rejects the rejection shape.
findings.remedy: Decode MutationOutcome rejections in the Kotlin controller using the same code-to-message table and uncertain/busy rules as TypeScript. Remove the reservation when the rejection is fresh and not busy. Add a Kotlin test that sends rejected invalid-input and busy replies.

obligations.evidence: No removalConfirmation implementation or Delete/Discard confirmation code is in the supplied files. The mutation fixture only records the remove request field set, the original ticket and ticket-only cleanup calls, and none of the removal tests are in the evidence.

The Kotlin ConnectionMutationControllerTest and the mutation fixture exercise frozen-attempt, same-ticket replay, expiry and lost-reply unknown behaviour, including no repeated create via ticket and mutation counters. The controllers (TypeScript and Kotlin) and the Kotlin record store are not supplied, and no test was run.

Tests show project-service ownership, project disposal and a fresh project with no inherited records. The service, panel, configurable, plugin.xml and gateway code are not supplied. The test backend asserts lane opening happens off the dispatch thread.

Tests for before, after, pending and malformed lost-reply faults expect unknown, then reconcile via status or identical same-ticket replay, with no second ticket and no changed payload. The production controller is not supplied and the tests were not run.

For draft tests, test-controller.ts and ConnectionDraftTests.kt check key, epoch, view generation and draft revision before publishing, and retain the reservation and source until a reachable reply. List-reply staleness is not in the supplied files. The one defect found is the Kotlin rejection-handling gap.
The fixture checks that removeState and retryCleanup receive only the original ticket. The removal production code and the tests that assert source preservation are not supplied.
There is no sc6 consumer code in the evidence. The fixture exposes removal handlers and a sourcePreserved stat, but the removal consumer and its tests are absent.

Supplied files are client controllers, tests and fixtures only. The fixture imports daemon modules, but only as a test peer. The full diff, and whether any adjacent-story contract is reimplemented, cannot be judged.

PersistentDaemonLane and UnixSocketDaemonRpc.kt are not supplied. The tests only use PersistentDaemonLane.open/request/close/awaitClosed/isClosed, with no framing or partial-write tests in the evidence.
The TypeScript signed mutation gateway is not supplied, and CM-S5-OUTCOME-TS is not in the evidence. Only the Kotlin outcome test wrapper and fixture are visible.

ConnectionDraftTests.kt and its tests cover stale tuples, cancel on view change, disposal suppression and EDT-delivery tests. The Kotlin rejected-outcome handling does not match TypeScript, see the finding. Session-service wiring and execution results are absent.
No plugin.xml, ConnectionsConfigurable or ManageConnectionsAction is in the supplied files.

No VS Code UI evidence is supplied. The fixture has a test-only live-ui mode, but no screenshots or results are in the evidence. The user states manual 0.5.23 testing was done but not individually documented, so I do not treat it as proven.
The fixture byte-compares a source CSV (sourcePreserved) for the mutation/removal flows. No SQL, KV or both-client live evidence is supplied, and SQL Server is pending by user authorization.

limitations: Only the supplied diff fragments were reviewed. Production mutation/removal controllers, ConnectionsSessionService, ConnectionDraft, ConnectionProtocol, PersistentDaemonLane, the TypeScript wire decoders and mutation gateway, plugin.xml and the UI panels were not supplied.
No tests or builds were run, so I treated nothing as passing.
Not assessed: ConnectionMutationBackend.kt and connection-test-server.ts (referenced by tests, not in the evidence), and fixtures/connection-junit.js beyond its call sites.

A possible lock-order inversion between ConnectionDraftTests.stop (lock, then r, then subscription.close) and the draft's own monitor cannot be judged without the ConnectionDraft source. I did not raise it as a defect.
The user's recorded decisions (VS Code and JetBrains only, runtime management default-on with releaseEnabled false, manual and deferred test statuses) were not reopened.

jetbrains-plugin/.../connections/ConnectionDraft.kt, to check the lock order of onChange subscription close against edit callbacks.
Kotlin and TypeScript removal/mutation controllers (including removalConfirmation and the OperationTicket record store) for the unverified removal and ticket obligations.
jetbrains-plugin/.../daemon/PersistentDaemonLane.kt and UnixSocketDaemonRpc.kt, with their transport tests, for plan t5.
plugin.xml, ConnectionsConfigurable and ManageConnectionsAction, with the entry tests, for plan t21.
